headline: Twenty-one stations behind the Hillcrest repeater went quiet — one shared path, not 21 faults — and four only because we stopped listening.
author: Claude — the first bulletin, from the facts and the receptions

notes: Receptions, carriers, the base station's settings and its log read through the Supabase connector.

caveats: One base station hears all of this. Whether Hillcrest or our receiver explains the overnight drop cannot be settled from its readings alone.
The Bureau's own base stations may still be hearing the Hillcrest stations; Flood-Net cannot see them.
Kunghur and Dunbible Creek report batteries of 9.5 to 10 V and keep transmitting — more likely a different scale on file than flat batteries.
Five transmitters measured 15 to 18 ppm high only through stick 2, which ran without a frequency correction until 10:34 Saturday; that is the receiver's error and is left out.

scenes.title: Good morning
scenes.say: Good morning, and welcome to Sunday's numbers. Unsettled over Logan: twenty-one stations behind one repeater went quiet — one cause, not twenty-one site visits, which is the kind of variance I like.

scenes.title: A low over Logan and Ipswich
scenes.sub: 21 quiet stations, every one in Hillcrest's pass ranges
scenes.say: Here's the system. Twenty-one stations that keep a schedule — Henderson Creek, Loamside, Beaudesert and the rest — dropped out one by one, from late Saturday morning into the small hours. Every one is in the Hillcrest repeater's pass ranges. Hillcrest itself is still on air: its own battery report came in at half past midnight, a steady 13.1 volts.

scenes.title: Whose copies are they?
scenes.sub: the carrier on the corrupted copies
scenes.say: Alex Chen, on the radio side. Every transmitter has a carrier of its own — a fingerprint. Lyons AL came through corrupted 41 times this week, and two repeaters pass Lyons. Of the copies with a measured carrier, eight of nine came on Hillcrest's, as strong as the clean ones. Across the week, half of what Hillcrest re-sent arrived corrupted.
scenes.verdict: Clear copies, wrong bits: the corruption enters at Hillcrest — its receiver, or something at the site that it hears.

scenes.title: Our end of the line
scenes.sub: each channel, hour by hour, against its usual
scenes.say: Now our end. At six past ten on Saturday the base station's first stick was retuned, and it logged that it was falling behind and dropping samples. Its uploads have trailed by a minute since, not seven seconds. 152.400 was listened to only until a quarter to six. And from four this morning, every channel on stick 1 thinned at once.

scenes.title: Two explanations
scenes.sub: and what would tell them apart
scenes.say: So: four of the twenty-one reach us only on 152.400 — they're quiet because we stopped listening. For the other seventeen, two explanations, and the readings can't separate them yet. Hillcrest may be going deaf: still transmitting, passing on less of what it hears and corrupting much of it. Or our receiver is losing the weaker relays. Both may be true.

items.text: Four — Dunwich, Coulson Crossing, Nindooinbah Dam, Lumeah — reach us only on 152.400 MHz, not listened to since 17:47 Saturday.
Hillcrest: what it relays thinned all Saturday and nearly stopped at 4 am; half of this week's re-sends came through corrupted.
Our base station: uploads a minute behind since Saturday's retune, and every stick 1 channel down by two-thirds or more since 4 am.
What would tell them apart: the stations returning when stick 1 is set back as it was — or the Bureau's own base stations still hearing them.

scenes.title: Fingerprints a step off
scenes.sub: two transmitters 2.3–2.5 kHz high, day after day
scenes.say: A fingerprint check. All but one of the fleet sits within two and a half parts per million — most within a quarter. Lake Manchester and ALERT2 source 10315 sit two and a half kilohertz high, day after day — about sixteen parts per million. No ageing crystal does that; it looks more like a radio set a step off its channel. One to check, not to drive to.

items.name: ALERT2 10315
items.note: +2.5 kHz on three days; no station on file has it

scenes.title: Batteries
scenes.say: On to power. Three batteries fell off a cliff overnight: Upper Goomburra from 13.1 to 11.2 volts, Thornton School Road from 12.8 to 9.4, Priestdale to 11.3. A drop that sudden is more often a cell, a connection or the charger than a tired battery. Nindooinbah Dam is the slow one, about six days from 11.8.

items.name: Thornton (School Rd) AL
items.note: 12.8 V five nights running, then 9.4 V

scenes.title: Worth a look today
scenes.say: So, worth a look today: the Hillcrest path and our stick 1, together. Upper Goomburra's battery. Lake Manchester's frequency when someone's passing. And good news: thirty-three stations the server had called silent were heard again — Cressbrook Dam, Borumba Dam and Jimna among them.

items.text: The Hillcrest path and our stick 1 — one of them, or both, explains 17 quiet stations.
Upper Goomburra AL — battery 11.2 V last night, after 13.1 V the night before.
Lake Manchester AL — transmitting 2.3 kHz high; worth checking what its radio is set to.
Heard again: 33 stations the server had called silent — Cressbrook Dam, Borumba Dam, Couran Point and Jimna among them.

scenes.title: That’s the network
scenes.say: That's the network this morning: one repeater, one receiver, and twenty-one stations that are probably fine where they stand. Every dollar has a job. Back tomorrow.
